These adjustments control the gain setting of the analog amplifiers in the scanner hardware. The gain settings of these amplifiers determine the exposure of the Red, Green and Blue channels.
The software normally determines these settings without user interaction. However when you have a film that has extreme conditions such as over or under exposure,

there is a chance to produce better scan result by changing these settings manually.  Please note that use of this control may provide unexpected results. 0The units are displayed in EV (Exposure Value).

When you press the "Calibrate" button, a scanner calibration is performed. The scanner calibration is automatically performed any time the film is changed.
If you do not change the film for a long period of time, and if the scanner environment, such as room temperature, is changing rapidly, the scanner calibration may drift.
This may result in banding noise on the scanned image. Please press the calibration button if you notice this phenomenon and then rescan your image.

CleanImage automatically fixes defects on the film surface, such as scratches and/or dust. As a result of this process, the scanning speed will be slower. If the resulting scans look soft, try the "Sharpen" mode.
